title: Harden BTC monthly candle fetching with reliable OHLCV sources and provider-agnostic UI copy

requirements.summary: Switch monthly (1M) BTC candle fetching to a fast, free public OHLCV source that returns monthly candles directly while keeping the Candle format stable.
acceptanceCriteria: The BTC chart page loads and renders monthly candles without showing the "Failed to Load Data" state under normal network conditions.
Monthly candle data is fetched from a free, public endpoint that does not require an API key, and the app no longer relies on aggregating daily prices into monthly candles as its primary path.

The returned dataset is normalized into the existing Candle interface (time in ms; open/high/low/close numbers; volume present even if 0) and remains compatible with BtcMonthlyChart and liquidity model computations.

file_operations.description: Add provider-agnostic normalization helpers to convert a direct monthly OHLCV payload into the existing Candle interface (time in ms; numeric OHLC; volume always present, defaulting to 0 when missing) while keeping existing Candle and any existing converters stable.

Replace the CoinGecko daily-to-monthly aggregation as the primary path with a direct monthly (1M) OHLCV fetch from a free public source (no API key) and normalize results into the existing Candle[] shape consumed by BtcMonthlyChart and liquidity computations.

requirements.summary: Add resilient client-side fetch behavior for monthly candles (timeout/abort, clearer error classification, and automatic fallback to a secondary free public source).
acceptanceCriteria: If the primary endpoint request fails (network error, non-2xx, invalid payload, or timeout), the app automatically attempts at least one fallback free public endpoint before showing an error state.
Requests have a reasonable timeout using AbortController so the UI does not hang indefinitely on slow responses.
When all attempts fail, the error state remains user-friendly (no raw stack traces), and the Retry button triggers a fresh attempt (including fallback behavior).

file_operations.description: Create reusable fetch helpers for market-data requests, including AbortController-based timeouts, basic response validation, and error classification suitable for user-friendly messaging (no provider names).

Implement sequential attempts (primary then at least one fallback) using the new fetch utilities; validate payloads before normalization; on total failure throw a concise, user-friendly Error message; ensure React Query refetch triggers a full fresh attempt including fallback behavior.

requirements.summary: Update BTC chart loading/error UI copy to be provider-agnostic and refer to “market data” generically.
acceptanceCriteria: The loading state text no longer says it is “Fetching monthly candles from CoinGecko...”.
All user-facing text remains in English.
The error state continues to provide a clear message and a working Retry action.

file_operations.description: Update the Loading and default Error copy to reference “market data” generically (no provider names) while keeping the existing Retry button behavior intact.
